title: Gewürztraminer
description: Also called Traminer Aromatico in Italy. Lychee, rose and ginger: the most recognisable aromatic white grape.
L: Gewürztraminer gives deep golden wines with intense aromas of lychee, rose petals, ginger, Turkish delight and sometimes smoke. It's full-bodied, low in acidity and high in alcohol, often 13.5 to 14.5%. Even dry versions can seem sweet because of the perfume. Few grapes are easier to recognise.

Gewürz means spice in German. The grape is an aromatic, pink-skinned mutation of Savagnin, the Traminer family, named after Tramin, or Termeno, in Alto Adige, Italy. Its pink to red skin gives white wines a deep golden colour. It buds early and ripens to high sugar.
What does Gewürz mean in German?
Gewürz means spice, for its spicy aromatic character.

Look for deep gold colour, an explosive nose of lychee and rose, and a full, oily palate with low acidity. A slight bitterness on the finish is common. If you smell lychee, it's almost certainly Gewürztraminer.
Gewürztraminer usually has very high acidity.
Not true. It's typically low in acidity, which is why it can feel heavy.
Gewürztraminer smells of lychee, rose and ginger
It's a pink-skinned mutation of the Traminer family from Tramin
It's full-bodied, low in acidity and high in alcohol

Gewürztraminer's most famous home is Alsace, where it's about 20% of plantings and one of the four noble grapes allowed in Grand Cru wines. Alsace's dry, sunny autumns, in the rain shadow of the Vosges, ripen it fully. Germany, Alto Adige, Austria, New Zealand and Oregon also grow it.
Alsace: one of four noble grapes

Gewürztraminer needs a cool climate: in heat, it ripens too fast, losing what little acidity it has and becoming flabby and oily. It buds early, so it's sensitive to spring frost, and it's prone to disease. Picking time is critical: too early, the aromas are weak; too late, the acidity disappears.
Match each region to its Gewürztraminer.
In Alsace, a dry Gewürztraminer and a sweet one can look identical. Some producers use a sweetness scale on the back label; check it before you buy.
Why must Gewürztraminer be picked at exactly the right time?
Too early, aromas are weak; too late, acidity disappears
The window between aromatic ripeness and flabbiness is narrow.
Alsace is Gewürztraminer's most famous home
It needs a cool climate to keep balance
Picking time decides aroma and freshness
Explain why Gewürztraminer is so aromatic
Compare it with other aromatic grapes

Gewürztraminer's perfume comes mainly from terpenes, aromatic compounds also found in flowers and citrus. Geraniol smells of rose, linalool of flowers, and cis-rose oxide, found at high levels in Gewürztraminer, of lychee and rose. These compounds sit mostly in the skins and grow as the grape ripens.

Gewürztraminer has some of the highest terpene levels of any grape, along with Muscat. Unlike thiols in Sauvignon Blanc, which form during fermentation, terpenes are present in the grape itself. Some are free and smell immediately; others are bound to sugars and released slowly by enzymes, during fermentation and ageing.
Which compound gives Gewürztraminer its lychee aroma?
Cis-rose oxide is found at high levels in Gewürztraminer, smelling of lychee and rose.

Because terpenes sit in the skins, some winemakers give Gewürztraminer a few hours of skin contact before pressing to extract more aroma. Too much, though, adds bitterness and phenolic grip. Muscat, Torrontés and Viognier are other terpene-rich grapes, with their own aroma profiles.
Which grapes are rich in terpenes?
Cabernet's aromas come mostly from pyrazines and esters, not terpenes.
Terpenes like cis-rose oxide and geraniol give its perfume
They sit in the skins, free or bound to sugars
Muscat and Torrontés are other terpene-rich grapes
Explain why Gewürztraminer suits sweet styles

Alsace's Vendanges Tardives, VT, means late harvest. Grapes stay on the vine into late autumn, concentrating sugar. Gewürztraminer VT needs a minimum potential alcohol of about 15.3%, around 257 g/l of sugar at harvest. The wines can be dry, off-dry or sweet, rich and intensely perfumed.

Sélection de Grains Nobles, SGN, is made from berries affected by noble rot, picked one by one. Minimum sugar is higher, about 18.2% potential alcohol for Gewürztraminer. SGN wines are lusciously sweet, with honey, candied fruit and spice, and can age for decades.
Order these Alsace Gewürztraminer styles from least to most concentrated.
Later picking and noble rot concentrate sugar further.

Gewürztraminer's high natural sugar and intense aroma suit late harvest styles. Its weakness, low acidity, is a challenge: the best VT and SGN come from top sites and vintages where acidity is preserved. Without it, the wines can feel heavy.
High sugar, but acidity is key
What is Sélection de Grains Nobles made from?
SGN uses botrytised berries, selected one by one.
Vendanges Tardives is late harvest, dry to sweet
SGN uses noble rot berries and is lusciously sweet
Acidity decides the best sweet Gewürztraminer

Gewürztraminer's perfume and body suit mildly spiced Asian dishes, especially Thai, Indian and Moroccan food, ideally with a touch of sweetness. In Alsace, it's the classic match for Munster, a pungent washed-rind cheese. It also suits foie gras, smoked salmon and ginger.

Serve at 10 to 12 degrees, not too cold, or the aromas close up. Most dry Gewürztraminer is best within three to five years. Grand Cru wines age 10 years or more; VT and SGN can age for decades, gaining honey and dried fruit.
Which cheese is Alsace's classic match for Gewürztraminer?
Pair an off-dry Gewürztraminer with Thai green curry. The touch of sugar calms the chilli, and the ginger and lime echo the wine.
Gewürztraminer should be served ice cold to bring out its aromas.
Not true. Too cold, its aromas close up. About 10 to 12 degrees is better.
Gewürztraminer suits mild spice, Munster and foie gras
Grand Crus and sweet styles age for decades
Not true. Its low acidity is its main challenge.
Which compounds contribute to Gewürztraminer's aroma?
Pyrazines are typical of Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet.
Alsace's late harvest wines are labelled Vendanges ____.
Gewürztraminer smells of lychee, rose and ginger
Alsace makes it dry, late harvest and SGN
